search_log: Searched "End Game David Baldacci excerpt chapter 1 publisher", "first chapter", and author/publisher-site variants; the Hachette and Pan Macmillan pages supplied synopsis material but no readable excerpt.
Searched "End Game David Baldacci point of view third person narration" and "narrator"; found and opened an explicit whole-book third-person description on Lars Emmerich's thriller site.
Searched exact opening lines and "End Game David Baldacci read sample ebook"; opened sustained chapter 1 and chapter 2 text showing third-person narration with clearly local first-person thoughts.

Checked Google Books, Google Play, Apple Books, Open Library, and the separately issued First Six Chapters preview; Google Books returned a 403 when opened, while the other accessible catalog pages did not expose diagnostic prose.

Searched exact interior quote fragments including "He instantly knew what Patti had done", "Vee-one meant the aircraft", and "Both Robie and Reel tensed"; no additional authoritative passage source was found.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person: sustained web prose externally narrates Robie while entering his knowledge and perceptions, and an explicit secondary description identifies the novel's point of view as third person. The Goodreads evidence independently corroborates this through extended scene beats that narrate Robie, Reel, Claire, and others externally. Numerous I and you forms are dialogue, aphorism, or local internal thought rather than autonomous first- or second-person sections. No evidence of a sustained person alternation was found. Confidence is medium because the readable prose source and explicit POV description are Tier C rather than authorized Tier A or structural Tier B evidence.
